_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. August, and the afternoons are hot. This week’s question is the one that keeps threshing crews safe: will those puffy clouds blow up into a thunderstorm, and when do you get everybody indoors?

replies.back: Don’t sound so pleased. A storm doesn’t care how much you’ve studied.

turns.them: How a heap becomes a storm, how to feel one coming, and how to count the distance to its lightning. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions, and mind the thunder.
And thirty minutes after the last thunder before anybody goes back out. Two lessons left, for autumn and winter.
